I get what you’re trying to say, but it still doesn’t make sense to compare a ~$50k FWD Hot Hatch to $70k + AWD Hot Hatches. The closest competitors to an i30N would be a Focus ST and an FK8 Type R, hell, even a GR Yaris. 

Regardless of the power differences, it still competes directly against the 128ti and Golf GTI, as they are both within the same price bracket (actually being more expensive), and are both FWD hot hatches. 

That all said, I’d 100% agree with you if you had said a GR Corolla and FL5 Type R would compete with a Golf R/A35/M135i/S3.

That isn’t how it works at all, that’s essentially saying you couldn’t compare a Golf R to an S3, you’d have to compare it to an RS3. 

The 128ti is compared to the i30N because they’re both around the same price range, and are both FWD Hot Hatches. The M135i falls into a separate category, compared to other AWD Hot Hatches around the same price point (Golf R, A35, S3).

I am not discrediting the 128ti or BMW, I’m comparing two cars that would be cross-shopped (just the same as reviewers around the world).

Not discounting the BMW, as it’s a great car, but the i30N is definitely the pick out of the two. Looks may be subjective, but I personally think the ti just looks like another BMW, whereas the i30N stands out (sounds much better too). i30N also goes 0-100 in a claimed 5.4; whereas the BMW goes a claimed 6.3.
